Which of these four came first?
Assembly language (founded 1949) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these was founded earliest?
Pascal (programming language) (founded 1970) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the physicist from these four.
Norman Ramsey Jr. is a physicist.
Which one below is best known as a chemist?
Mai Thi Nguyen-Kim is a chemist. Mai Thi Nguyen-Kim is a German chemist, science communicator, television presenter and YouTuber.
What is the atomic number of Californium?
Californium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Cf and atomic number 98.
In what year was Robert F. Kennedy Jr. born?
Robert F. Kennedy Jr.: A member of the prominent Kennedy family, he is a son of Senator and US attorney general Robert F.
In what year did Thomas Edison die?
Thomas Edison: Thomas Alva Edison (February 11, 1847 – October 18, 1931) was an American inventor and businessman.
In what year was Sulfur discovered?
Sulfur (American spelling or sulphur (Commonwealth spelling) is a chemical element; it has symbol S and atomic number 16.
Diazepam: Pfizer. Diazepam, sold under the brand name Valium among others, is a medication of the benzodiazepine family that acts as an anxiolytic.
In which country is Dassault Mirage 2000?
Dassault Mirage 2000: France. Work on what would become the Mirage 2000 originated with the "Delta 1000" project launched in 1972.
Who is credited with discovering Ruthenium?
Ruthenium: Karl Ernst Claus. Ruthenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ru and atomic number 44.
Who is credited with discovering Aniline?
Aniline: Otto Unverdorben. Aniline (From Portuguese: anil, meaning 'indigo shrub', and -ine indicating a derived substance) is an organic compound with the formula C6H5NH2.
Who is credited with discovering Lie group?
Lie group: Sophus Lie. Combining these two ideas, one obtains a continuous group where multiplying points and their inverses is continuous.
With the formula (CH3)2CO, this volatile solvent is produced by the millions of tonnes yearly, much of it to make precursors for plastics like bisphenol A — what is it?
Acetone (2-propanone or dimethyl ketone) is an organic compound with the formula (CH3)2CO.
The twelfth-brightest star in our night sky and the brightest in the constellation Aquila. It's one of the three vertices of the Summer Triangle asterism. Name this star.

Altair is the brightest star in the equatorial constellation of Aquila and the twelfth-brightest star in the night sky. It has the Bayer designation Alpha Aquilae, which is Latinised from α Aquilae and abbreviated Alpha Aql or α Aql.
The largest genus in the arum family with roughly 1,000 species, this flowering plant group is native to the Americas, ranging from northern Mexico down to northern Argentina — which genus?
Anthurium (Schott, 1829) is a genus of about 1,000 species of flowering plants, the largest genus of the arum family, Araceae.

This lung condition — the partial collapse of alveoli that reduces gas exchange, usually in just one lung — is a very common finding on chest X-rays, though it's technically distinct from a fluid-filled lung or a full pneumothorax — what is it?
Atelectasis is the partial collapse or closure of a lung resulting in reduced or absent gas exchange, more specifically the collapse of alveoli.
Native to Southeast Asia, the glossy heart-shaped leaves of this evergreen vine are chewed together with areca nut — name the plant?
Betel (Piper betle) is a species of flowering plant in the pepper family Piperaceae, native to Southeast Asia.
Located in the head in most animals with nervous systems, this organ receives sensory information, generates thought and cognition, and coordinates the body's muscles and glands — name the organ?
Brain is an organ that serves as the center of the nervous system in all vertebrate and most invertebrate animals.
This Italian mastiff breed once hunted big game and herded cattle, and today mostly serves as a guard dog and loyal companion — name the breed?
Cane Corso is an Italian breed of mastiff. It is usually kept as a companion dog or guard dog; it may also be used to protect livestock.
This English polymath is credited with inventing the first mechanical computer and designing an unrealized 'analytical engine' programmed using ideas borrowed from the Jacquard loom. Who is he?
Charles Babbage (26 December 1791 - 18 October 1871) was an English polymath.
Almost instantly after a vessel is injured, platelets swarm and fibrin cross-links to turn blood from liquid to gel, stopping the leak so repair can begin. What's the name for this clotting process?
Coagulation is the process by which blood changes from a liquid to a gel forming a blood clot.
Which vanilla-scented, benzopyrone lactone compound acts as a plant's chemical defense against predators and, via its derivatives, gave rise to the anticoagulant warfarin?
Coumarin is an aromatic organic chemical compound with formula C9H6O2.

This condition's four subtypes include one caused by kidneys that don't respond to a hormone called vasopressin and another linked to excessive fluid intake from a damaged thirst mechanism — what is it?
Diabetes insipidus (DI) is a condition characterized by large amounts of dilute urine and increased thirst.
Born in Dublin in 1869 into an old Anglo-Irish scientific family, she's considered the very first woman to work as a medical physicist — who was she?
Edith Anne Stoney (6 January 1869 - 25 June 1938) was an Irish physicist.
This flowering plant in the family Erythroxylaceae is one of just two species cultivated for their alkaloid-rich leaves — what is its scientific name?
Erythroxylum coca is a species of flowering plant in the family Erythroxylaceae.

Species in the stinging genus Solenopsis are sometimes confused with unrelated weaver insects in Southeast Asia that share their reddish color and painful bite — what's the common name for this group?
Fire ant are several species of ants in the genus Solenopsis, which includes over 200 species.
Its name literally means 'Earth writing,' and it explores not just where things are but how they changed and came to be across the planet — what field is it?
Geography (from Ancient Greek geographia; combining ge 'Earth' and graphein 'write', lit. 'Earth writing') is the study of the lands, features, inhabitants, and phenomena of planet Earth.

This small, hardy aquarium fish native to northeast South America gives birth to live young rather than laying eggs, and now ranks among the world's most widely kept tropical species — what fish is it?
Guppy (Poecilia reticulata), also known as the millionfish or rainbow fish, is a member of the family Poeciliidae and, akin to most New World members of the family, is classified as a livebearer.
This field studies the methods historians use — their sources, techniques, and theoretical approaches — in turning the past into an academic discipline — what's this field of study called?
Historiography is the study of the methods used by historians in developing history as an academic discipline.
This medieval Arab scholar, considered a forerunner of modern sociology and economics, wrote his most famous work, an introduction to history known as the Muqaddimah, in just six months — who is he?
Ibn Khaldun (27 May 1332 - 17 March 1406, 732-808 AH) was an Arab scholar, historian, philosopher, and sociologist.
This Brussels chemist ran a famous five-year willow tree experiment and coined the word 'gas' from the Greek for chaos — who was he?
Jan Baptist van Helmont (12 January 1580 - 30 December 1644) was a chemist, physiologist, and physician from Brussels.
This Hungarian-American biochemist spent years pushing past skepticism to lay the groundwork for mRNA vaccines, winning a 2023 Nobel alongside Drew Weissman. Who is she?

Katalin Karikó (born 17 January 1955) is a Hungarian and American biochemist who specializes in ribonucleic acid (RNA)-mediated mechanisms, particularly in vitro-transcribed messenger RNA (mRNA) for protein replacement therapy.
Named for the German city where it was bred in the mid-19th century, this is a large German dog breed — which breed?
Leonberger is a German breed of large dog. The breed name derives from that of the city of Leonberg, in Baden-Württemberg, where it was bred in the mid-nineteenth century.
Native to Afghanistan and Iran but long grown in Europe, this herb's leaves, roots, and seeds are all used in cooking, tasting like a more intense mix of celery and parsley — what is it?
Lovage (Levisticum officinale) is a perennial plant, the sole species in the genus Levisticum in the family Apiaceae, subfamily Apioideae.
Cold-sensitive and tasting of sweet pine and citrus, this kitchen herb is so close to its cousin that in parts of the Middle East the two names are used interchangeably with oregano. What is it?
This Cuban engineer-turned-politician became his country's top leader in 2021, making him the first head of Cuba since the 1959 revolution who isn't a member of the Castro family — who is he?

Miguel Díaz-Canel (Latin American; born 20 April 1960) is a Cuban politician and engineer who has served as the 8th First Secretary of the Communist Party of Cuba and the top leader of Cuba since 2021.
Diagnosed after a speech assessment, this condition can stem from psychological trauma or a neurological disorder and isn't always permanent — what is it called?
Muteness is defined as an absence of speech, with or without an ability to hear the speech of others.

Made from unleavened dough rolled flat and then cut, stretched, or extruded into long strips, this staple food appears across cultures — in Italian cuisine, it goes by an entirely different name. What is it, generically?
Noodle are a type of food typically made from unleavened dough which is rolled flat and cut, stretched, or extruded into long strips or strings.
Often silent at first, this disease arises from an ovary or nearby structures and announces itself only later with bloating, pelvic pain, and abdominal swelling — what is it?
Ovarian cancer is a cancerous tumor of an ovary.
This flowering plant is the sole genus in its own botanical family and ranges from knee-high herbaceous perennials to woody shrubs over ten feet tall — what plant is it?
Peony is any flowering plant in the genus Paeonia, the only genus in the family Paeoniaceae.

This roundworm is one of the most common intestinal parasites in humans, causing a condition sometimes called oxyuriasis after the family it belongs to, and has also been found in bonnet macaques — what's the parasite?
Pinworm (parasite) (species Enterobius vermicularis), also known as threadworm (in the United Kingdom, Australia and New Zealand) or seatworm, is a parasitic worm.

An Italian chemist and Auschwitz survivor, he wrote a celebrated memoir of his year in the camp and later a book of stories each named for a chemical element, hailed as the best science book ever — who was he?
Primo Levi (31 July 1919 - 11 April 1987) was a Jewish Italian chemist, partisan, Holocaust survivor and writer.
This Indian Air Force pilot became the first Indian ever to travel to space, flying aboard a Soviet Soyuz mission in 1984 — who is he?
Rakesh Sharma (born 13 January 1949) is an Indian cosmonaut and a pilot of the Indian Air Force.
This woody perennial flowering plant, genus Rosa in the family Rosaceae, includes over 300 species and tens of thousands of cultivars, with sharp prickles on many stems — name the flower?
Rose is either a woody perennial flowering plant of the genus Rosa, in the family Rosaceae, or the flower it bears.
This marine plant group includes kelp, captures carbon, and generates over half of the planet's oxygen — what is it called?
Seaweed refers to thousands of species of macroscopic, multicellular, marine algae.
This discipline scientifically examines human society, scaling from micro-level individual interactions up to macro-level social systems — what is it?

Sociology is the scientific study of human society that focuses on society, human social behavior, patterns of social relationships, social interaction, and aspects of culture associated with everyday life.

This eye disorder causes the eyes to misalign when looking at an object; if it develops in childhood it often leads to a 'lazy eye,' while adult onset usually causes double vision instead — what condition is it?
Strabismus is an eye disorder in which the eyes do not properly align with each other when looking at an object.

The primary male sex hormone and androgen, this hormone plays a key role in developing male reproductive tissues and secondary sexual characteristics like muscle, bone mass, and body hair. What is this hormone?

Testosterone is the primary male sex hormone and androgen in males. It is associated with increased aggression, sex drive, dominance, courtship display, and a wide range of behavioral characteristics.
Following the instructions of the genetic code, which cellular process decodes mRNA outside the nucleus to assemble a polypeptide chain?
Translation (biology) is the process in biological cells in which proteins are produced using RNA molecules as templates.

Named after an 18th-century Italian physicist and first published in 1797, this phenomenon explains why fluid pressure drops as it speeds up through a narrower pipe section — powering wine aerators and vacuum ejectors. What is it called?
Venturi effect is the reduction in fluid pressure that results when a moving fluid speeds up as it is funneled from one section of a pipe to another, smaller section.

Extracted from birch wood and named for the Greek word for 'wood', this white crystalline sugar alcohol is more soluble in water than any other common sugar alcohol except sorbitol. Name the compound?
Xylitol is an organic compound with the formula HOCH(CH(OH)CH2OH)2.
Taken by mouth, smeared as a cream, or injected, this antiviral medication is a frontline treatment for herpes simplex, chickenpox, and shingles. What is it?
Aciclovir: Antiviral medication used against herpes, chickenpox, and shingles.
A broad-spectrum benzimidazole drug, it clears out an alarming roll call of intestinal parasites — pinworm, hookworm, ascariasis, giardiasis and more. Which medication is it?
Commonly called buffalo, this large grazing mammal endemic to North America is one of just two living species in its genus, alongside a European cousin — what animal is it?
American bison: Species of bovid artiodactyl mammal.
Evolved from vespoid wasp ancestors in the Cretaceous, these insects are easily spotted by their elbowed antennae and slender, node-waisted bodies — what are they?
Ant: Family of insects. Nearly all ant colonies also have some fertile males called "drones" and one or more fertile females called "queens" (gynes).
Pinned by a boulder in a Utah canyon in 2003, this mountaineer amputated his own forearm with a dull pocket knife to survive, later portrayed by James Franco in a film — who is he?
Derived from a Greek word meaning 'that which is thought worthy,' which term denotes a statement accepted as true without proof, serving as a starting point for further reasoning?
Axiom: Statement that is taken to be true.
A colorless, sweet-smelling liquid hiding in petroleum, this ring-shaped hydrocarbon helps give gasoline its distinctive aroma — what is it?
This crested songbird in the crow family sports a black, U-shaped collar and is known for hiding acorns to eat later — which eastern North American bird?
Blue jay: Species of bird. The blue jay (Cyanocitta cristata) is a passerine bird in the family Corvidae, native to eastern North America.
This rhythmic process of inhaling and exhaling delivers oxygen to the alveoli and removes carbon dioxide, with its per-minute rate counted as a vital sign — what is it?
Breathing: Process of moving air in and out of the lungs.
Found in chalk, limestone, eggshells, and pearls alike, this CaCO3 compound is also the active ingredient in agricultural lime and doubles as an antacid — what is it?
Calcium carbonate: Chemical compound. Materials containing much calcium carbonate or resembling it are described as calcareous.

Discovered as a single well-preserved skeleton in Argentina's Chubut Province in 1984, this short-snouted, lightly built predator belongs to a South American branch of large theropods — which dinosaur genus?
Carnotaurus: Genus of dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous period.
With independently swiveling eyes, a projectile tongue, and the ability to shift colors, this Old World lizard family is famous for camouflage — which reptile?
Chameleon: Family of reptiles. The members of this family are best known for their distinct range of colours, being capable of colour-shifting camouflage.
Named after a 17th-century English physician, this ring-shaped network of arteries supplies blood to the brain in humans and other vertebrates — what is it called?
Circle of Willis: Circulatory anastomosis that supplies blood to the brain and surrounding structures.
In this prolonged state of deep unconsciousness, a person cannot be awakened, shows no normal sleep-wake cycle, and may even be induced deliberately during general anesthesia — what is it?
Coma: State of unconsciousness. The person may experience respiratory and circulatory problems due to the body's inability to maintain normal bodily functions.
Smelling of vanilla but tasting bitter, which plant compound isn't itself an anticoagulant, though its derivatives inspired the blood-thinning drug warfarin?
This Zambian-born economist turned heads with four New York Times bestsellers, including "Dead Aid," which argues that foreign aid actually holds Africa back. Which author and life peer is it?
Dambisa Moyo, Baroness Moyo: Zambian-born economist (born February 1969)
Nicknamed 'dumb cane' because its poisonous sap can temporarily rob you of speech, this shade-tolerant tropical houseplant is native to the New World — which genus?
Dieffenbachia: Genus of plants. Dieffenbachia, commonly known as dumb cane or leopard lily, is a genus of tropical flowering plants in the family Araceae.
After co-founding a social media giant, this entrepreneur left in 2008 to launch the workplace software company Asana — who is he?
This stage of development begins right after fertilization, progressing from a single-celled zygote through a ball of cells called a morula — what is it called?
Embryo: Multicellular diploid eukaryote in its earliest stage of development.
This white solid is prized for binding iron and calcium ions into water-soluble complexes — handy for dissolving scale — and goes by a four-letter acronym. What is it?
In this common vision condition, distant objects appear sharp but close-up objects blur because light focuses behind the retina instead of on it - what is it?
Farsightedness: Eye condition in which light is focused behind instead of on the retina.
Sold under the brand name Luvox, this SSRI antidepressant treats OCD and other anxiety disorders, with milder side effects than most in its class except gastrointestinal ones — what drug is it?
Fluvoxamine: SSRI antidepressant. Fluvoxamine, sold under the brand name Luvox among others, is an antidepressant of the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) class.
Capable of living up to 177 years and weighing as much as 417 kilograms, which giant reptile — native to a chain of Pacific islands named for it — is the largest cold-blooded land animal alive today?
Galápagos tortoise: Species of reptile. The species comprises 15 subspecies (12 extant and 3 extinct).
Named from a Latin word for sword, this genus of cormous flowering plants in the iris family is sometimes called the 'sword lily' and is most diverse in South Africa's Cape region — which genus?
Gladiolus: Genus of perennial flowering plants. It is sometimes called the 'sword lily', but is usually called by its generic name (plural gladioli).
Known to the British as the Martlet, this American carrier-based fighter entered service in 1940 and remained the U.S. Navy's best fighter against the Mitsubishi Zero until mid-1943 — which aircraft?
Grumman F4F Wildcat: United States Navy World War II era fighter plane.
Native to North America, this genus of roughly 50 flowering plant species is better known by its common name — the sunflowers — and includes food crops for humans and livestock alike — which genus?

Helianthus: Genus of flowering plants, the sunflowers. Helianthus is a genus comprising around 50 species of annual and perennial flowering plants in the daisy family Asteraceae commonly known as sunflowers.
This extinct archaic human was the first to evolve a humanlike body and gait, the first to leave Africa for Asia and Europe, and the first to wield fire — who were they?
Homo erectus: Extinct species of archaic human. Homo erectus ( lit. 'upright man') is an extinct species of archaic human from the Pleistocene, spanning nearly 2 million years.
Distinct from a process that adds more cells, this one is an increase in the size of individual cells, like the uterus enlarging during pregnancy — what's it called?
Hypertrophy: Increase in the size of biological cells. Hypertrophy can lead to a relative increase in the volume of a tissue or organ, and contributes to the overall growth of an organism.

This neurological emergency is sudden bleeding directly into brain tissue or its fluid-filled cavities — not from a blocked vessel, but a burst one — causing anything from headache to sudden paralysis. What is it?
Intracerebral hemorrhage: Type of intracranial bleeding that occurs within the brain tissue itself.
Enlisting disguised as a man named 'Jean' on Bougainville's expedition, this expert botanist became the first woman to circumnavigate the globe — who is she?
Jeanne Baret: French explorer, naturalist, botanist (1740–1807)

This Indian aerospace engineer led the nation's space agency as chairman and served as secretary of the Department of Space, after directing both the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre and the Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre — who is he?
Once a water retriever in Italy's Po Delta marshlands, this Italian dog breed later became prized for sniffing out truffles — which breed?
Lagotto Romagnolo: Italian breed of dog.
As a principal shareholder of L'Oréal, this French heiress was the richest woman in the world at the time of her death in 2017, worth $44.3 billion — who was she?
Liliane Bettencourt: French heiress, socialite and businesswoman (1922–2017)
Originating in 1993 and written in ANSI C, this lightweight scripting language was designed to be embedded inside other applications — which language?
Lua: Lightweight programming language. Lua is a lightweight, high-level, multi-paradigm programming language designed mainly for embedded use in applications.
Sharing joints only with the temporal bones, this is the skull's lone movable bone, hosting the lower teeth and shrinking in size since humans began farming around 10,000 BCE — what is it called?
Mandible: Lower jaw bone. The mandible hosts the lower teeth (their depth delineated by the alveolar process).

This elephant-sized extinct genus of South American ground sloths, whose type species weighed up to four tonnes, was first identified from a fossil found on an Argentine riverbank in 1787 — which genus?
Megatherium: Genus of extinct ground sloth. The first (holotype) specimen of Megatherium americanum was discovered in 1787 on the bank of the Luján River in what is now northern Argentina.
North of the Arctic Circle in summer, this phenomenon keeps the sky lit long after the clock strikes twelve — what is it called?
Midnight sun: Natural phenomenon when daylight lasts for a whole day.
Sold under the brand name Singulair, this asthma medication blocks leukotriene D4 in the lungs but received a UK black box warning in 2019 over neuropsychiatric side effects — what is it?
Montelukast: Medication used in asthma or COPD.
This genus of venomous elapid snakes across Africa and Asia is home to the 'true cobras' — after a 2009 taxonomic revision folded in two other genera, it now contains 38 species — which genus?
Naja: Genus of snakes. Until recently, the genus Naja had 20 to 22 species, but it has undergone several taxonomic revisions in recent years, so sources vary greatly.
Colourless and odourless, this element pairs with itself to form a diatomic gas that makes up about 78% of the air you're breathing — what is it?
Nitrogen: Chemical element with atomic number 7 (N)

The most widely cultivated species of its genus, this bulb vegetable counts garlic, leeks and chives among its close relatives, and the shallot was reclassified as merely a variety of it in 2011 — what is it?
Onion: Bulbous vegetable. The shallot is a botanical variety of the onion which was classified as a separate species until 2011.
Nicknamed the 'scaly anteater,' this nocturnal mammal is covered in keratin scales and slurps up ants and termites with a long tongue — which animal?
Pangolin: Mammals of the order Pholidota.
Native to Asia, Europe, and western North America, this flowering shrub's fragrant blooms last just 7 to 10 days each spring — which plant?
Peony: Genus of flowering plants in the family Paeoniaceae.
This healthcare profession uses patient education and hands-on interventions to prevent, treat, and restore mobility, with specialties from sports medicine to pediatrics — which field?
Physical therapy: Profession that helps a disabled person function in everyday life.
Built from many linked simple sugars and including starch, glycogen, and cellulose among its examples, this class of carbohydrate is the most abundant in our food — what is it called?
Polysaccharide: Long carbohydrate polymers such as starch, glycogen, cellulose, and chitin.
This thorny European shrub's tart fruit gives sloe gin its name in Britain, while its wood becomes the classic Irish walking stick — what is it?
Prunus spinosa: Species of flowering plant in the rose family.
Domesticated in Asia, this crunchy root vegetable in the mustard family owes its peppery bite to compounds like glucosinolate — what vegetable is it?
Radish: Root vegetable of the Brassicaceae family. The radish (Raphanus sativus or Raphanus raphanistrum subsp. sativus) is a flowering plant in the mustard family, Brassicaceae.

Grown for its fleshy, edible stalks since before the 18th century in Europe and Scandinavia, this plant's broad triangular leaves are actually poisonous due to their high oxalic acid content. What is it?
Rhubarb: Species of herbaceous perennial plant with fleshy, sour edible stalks.
First identified in Wuhan in late 2019 and once provisionally called 2019-nCoV, this positive-sense RNA virus is the one that causes COVID-19 — what's its official name?
SARS-CoV-2: Virus that causes COVID-19. The virus previously had the provisional name 2019 novel coronavirus (2019-nCoV), and has also been called human coronavirus 2019 (HCoV-19 or hCoV-19).
A month or so of a diet starved of vitamin C brings on this old deficiency disease — fatigue, sore limbs, and bleeding gums among its hallmarks. What is its scorbutic name?
Scurvy: Disease resulting from a lack of vitamin C.
Named after a Native American war chief, this four-blade, twin-engine Army helicopter entered service in 1979 to replace the Bell UH-1 Iroquois — which aircraft is it?
Sikorsky UH-60 Black Hawk: Series of military utility transport helicopters.
Native to East Asia and the world's most-grown legume, this crop becomes everything from edamame and tofu to soy sauce, nattō and tempeh — what is it?
Soybean: Legume grown for its edible bean.
Named from Greek words for 'twisted' and 'grain,' this genus of spherical bacteria divides along a single axis to form chains, unlike its grape-cluster-forming cousins — coined in 1877, what is it?
Streptococcus: Genus of bacteria. In 1984, many bacteria formerly grouped in the genus Streptococcus were separated out into the genera Enterococcus and Lactococcus.
Marketed under the brand name Flomax, this alpha-blocker medication treats enlarged prostate symptoms and helps ease the passage of kidney stones — which drug?
Tamsulosin: Medication. Tamsulosin, sold under the brand name Flomax among others, is a medication used to treat symptomatic benign prostatic hyperplasia and chronic prostatitis.

Born from 19th-century efforts to make steam engines more efficient — thanks largely to French physicist Sadi Carnot — this branch of physics is governed by four fundamental laws relating heat, work, and energy. What is it?

Thermodynamics: Physics of heat, work, and temperature. The initial application of thermodynamics to mechanical heat engines was quickly extended to the study of chemical compounds and chemical reactions.

Once dismissed as rare and bizarre, this childhood-onset disorder pairs multiple motor tics with at least one vocal tic, often heralded by a premonitory urge the person can briefly suppress — what's it called?
Tourette syndrome: Neurodevelopmental disorder involving motor and vocal tics.
Often caused by poor circulation or prolonged pressure on the skin, this open sore — also known as a bedsore when linked to immobility — can destroy tissue down to the fat layer. What is it called?
This ability to detect light and turn it into an image of one's surroundings can occur via daytime or night vision — what is it called?
Visual perception: Ability to interpret the surrounding environment using light in the visible spectrum.
Also called sallows or osiers, this genus of roughly 350 mostly deciduous tree and shrub species thrives on moist soil in cold, temperate regions — which plant?
Americium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for americium is Am. Americium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Am and atomic number 95.
The symbol for flerovium is Fl. Flerovium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Fl and atomic number 114.

In what year was Farrah Fawcett born?
Farrah Fawcett: Mary Ferrah Leni "Farrah" Fawcett (February 2, 1947 – June 25, 2009) was an American actress.
In what year was Angelina Jolie born?
Angelina Jolie ( joh-LEE; born Angelina Jolie Voight [ VOYT] on June 4, 1975) is an American actress, filmmaker, and humanitarian.
In what year was Viggo Mortensen born?
Viggo Mortensen: Viggo Peter Mortensen Jr. (Danish: [ˈviko ˈmɒːtn̩sn̩]; born October 20, 1958) is an American actor and filmmaker.
In what year was Marisa Tomei born?
Marisa Tomei (Italian: [toˈmɛi]; born December 4, 1964) is an American actress.

Steve Carell: Steven John Carell (born August 16, 1962) is an American actor and comedian.

Ryuichi Sakamoto: With his YMO bandmates Haruomi Hosono and Yukihiro Takahashi, Sakamoto influenced and pioneered a number of electronic music genres.
In what year was Han So-hee born?
Han So-hee: Lee So-hee (Korean: 이소희; born November 18, 1993), better known by the stage name Han So-hee (한소희), is a South Korean actress.
In what year was Hugh Laurie born?
Hugh Laurie: James Hugh Calum Laurie (born 11 June 1959) is an English actor, comedian, and musician.
In what year was Luke Evans born?
